arc: stat (raise counter rolls up) → announcement ('Solara announcing $400M' between colour-bar stacks) → announcement ('Series F' sheared bands) → stat (halftone valuation card) → stat ('$8.4B valuation' steps up) → transition ('The future of' over sky) → proof (future of work + customer-industry list) → benefit (agentic control plane line) → logo

scenes.title: Giant rolling-digit raise counter rising into frame
scenes.summary: A beige card inset on navy with the small Solara sphere mark and 'Solara' wordmark at centre. A huge '$39xM' number (digits ~490px tall, dark navy Inter) climbs up through the card while its last digit rolls 6→7→8→9 with a vertical motion smear; the tens and hundreds digits carry a fading smear in the first frames, and in the last two frames it shoots upward out of view. Under one second long.
scenes.build: Orthographic stage (kit.ts stage()) in composition pixels; each glyph ('$', '3', '9', one plane per ones digit 6-9, 'M') is its own text() plane so only the ones digit swaps. Vertical position comes from a per-frame lookup table (DOLLAR_TOP) measured off a reference; motion blur is the kit shader's one-axis gaussian (blur(m, 0, 22)), and clipTo() masks everything to the rounded card in world space.
scenes.reuse: Borrow the idea of a cropped, oversized counter with per-digit motion blur for a punchy number opener; change the glyphs and the VALUE/LEFT functions. Frame-table timings are reference-specific and very short, so retime to taste rather than copy the arrays.

scenes.title: 'Solara announcing $400M' squeezed between two growing stacks of colour bars
scenes.summary: On the beige card, rounded bars in green, orange, yellow and cyan grow in from the top and bottom edges one after another, stacking into two stepped pyramids that squeeze toward a small centred lockup 'Solara announcing' over '$400M'. At frame 68 the bars and type snap to a larger size, then the bars shear out sideways on an accelerating curve, top stack exiting right and bottom stack left.
scenes.build: Each bar is an SDF rounded-rect shader panel (kit.ts rect) with horizontal gaussian edge softness (uSoftX/uSoftY) standing in for motion blur. Bar edges and half-widths come from per-frame tables and keys() piecewise keyframes measured off a reference; the exit lerps edges toward fixed targets with a measured EXIT acceleration curve. Type is sized to exact ink widths with sizeForInk(); fonts are loaded inside the export's frame barrier via withFonts().
scenes.reuse: Strong graphic for a funding or launch headline: swap the four palette colours in brand.ts and the two strings. The stepped colour-bar framing and snap-scale is the idea; the per-frame tables are tuned to one reference, so you may prefer to regenerate them with simple eased keyframes.

scenes.title: 'Series F' repeated in five ruled bands that shear apart, centre turns to grass
scenes.summary: The beige card is divided by four thin grey rules into five horizontal bands, each showing 'Series F' in large grey Poppins clipped to its band; the outer bands are blurred more. The rows slide sideways in opposite directions (rows above left, below right, outer rows 1.8x as far), shearing the word apart. Near the end the centre band cuts to a green grassy-hills photo with the word turned white and a small white dot on the right.
scenes.build: Five copies of one text() mesh, each clipTo()'d to its band rectangle and blurred per row (BLUR = [9,5,0,5,9]); x positions come from measured keyframes ROW_UP/ROW_DOWN with the outer rows multiplied by OUTER. The grass is kit.ts image() with cover() fit clipped to the centre band and toggled on at GRASS_AT; tint() swaps the centre word to white.
scenes.reuse: Great for naming a round, version or product with a slit-scan/shear look: change the word, band count and the photo. Swap the grass for any image that relates to your brand. Keep the per-band clipping and graded blur — that's what sells it.

scenes.title: Halftone '$8.4B' on a card resolving solid, with a callout label
scenes.summary: A beige card fills the left ~60% of a navy frame with '$8.4B' set huge in grey Inter, rendered as a staggered halftone dot screen. A white hairline runs right from the card's edge to a white dot and the label 'Solara Valuation'. Halfway through, the number snaps from halftone to solid type.
scenes.build: kit.ts shader mode 3: the text texture is sampled at the centre of each cell of a brick-offset dot grid in world space and drawn as a dot (halftone(m, on, 14)). Switching to solid is just halftone(big, false). Callout is two rect() panels plus text().
scenes.reuse: Use the halftone-to-solid print effect on any hero number or word for an editorial feel; swap the figure, label and colours. Very short (27 frames), so lengthen it or pair it with a count-up.

scenes.title: '$8.4B valuation' on navy growing in three hard steps
scenes.summary: A navy panel on beige with 'Solara' small above a single white Poppins line '$8.4B valuation'. The two words drift apart slightly, then the whole line jumps bigger in three hard, unanimated steps while 'Solara' grows with it.
scenes.build: One group holding the two text() meshes; a STEPS table of measured ink boxes picks the current step by frame and sets a uniform scale and position, with keys() drift during the first step.
scenes.reuse: Only the stepped-scale beat is new here; it repeats the $8.4B message of the previous scene as a single text line. Borrow the hard-step scale jump as a rhythmic emphasis on a music hit, not the scene itself.

scenes.title: 'The future of' typed in mixed sans and serif italic over open sky
scenes.summary: A rounded sky-and-landscape photo, tinted cool blue and slightly dimmed, fills the frame. White text 'The future of' types glyph by glyph — 'The' and 'of' in Inter, 'future' in Instrument Serif italic — while the line slowly scales up ~19% and accelerates off to the left. It sets up the headline completed in the next scene.
scenes.build: The line is laid out glyph by glyph (one text() per character, measured with mixed styles so pen positions hold across the font switch) inside one group; visibility per glyph from a TYPED(frame) step function; scale and x from measured keyframes. Background is kit.ts image() with cover(), zoom and pan, uColor tint and uDim.
scenes.reuse: Reuse the mixed sans + italic serif typed line over a photo as a lead-in to a vision statement; change the words, which word gets the serif, and the image. It's the first half of a sentence, so pair it with a follow-up scene.

scenes.title: 'The future of work is on Solara' card snaps right as an industry list scrolls
scenes.summary: Full-frame landscape card with the headline 'The future of work is on Solara' (serif italic 'future', 'Solara' typing in) and a small 'Solara' label, drifting left. Then the landscape card snaps to the right two-thirds of the frame and a vertical list of rounded stat cards scrolls up on the left: big blue numbers with 'of the largest' and a category — '16 Manufacturing Companies', '12 Healthcare & Pharmacy Organizations', '12 Retailers', '10 Financial Services Firms', '9 Travel & Hospitality Companies', '8 Business Process Outsourcers'. The active card shows a full-bleed photo with white text and blue number; the others are pale ghosts, and the highlight advances five times.
scenes.build: Headline is per-word/per-letter text() meshes laid out from measured advances, clipped to whichever card box is current (CARD_FULL vs CARD_RIGHT at SPLIT_AT). The list is seven card groups (border, fill, photo, number, lead, lines) whose top edge is ACTIVE_TOP[frame] − PITCH × activeIndex, so the scroll is a measured per-frame table with eased advances; tint() greys inactive cards and only the active card's image() is visible.
scenes.reuse: A strong 'who uses us' / customer-segment proof beat: replace the STATS entries (number, category lines, card-*.jpg) and the headline words. The split layout — vision headline on an image card on the right, scrolling highlighted stat list on the left — transfers to any industries/use-cases/customers list. Retime ACTIVE_TOP if you change the count of cards.

scenes.title: Tagline rises word by word in extreme close-up, then pulls back to the full line
scenes.summary: A navy panel. The camera starts tight on the word 'agentic' filling much of the frame as words rise up from below one after another, each starting grey and brightening to white. It then pulls back smoothly to reveal the full two-line centred tagline 'The agentic control plane / for enterprises', and the white Solara sphere mark with 'Solara' fades in above it.
scenes.build: All words and the mark live in one group; the zoom is group scale = Z^(1 − z) (eased in log space so the pull reads at a constant rate) while the framed point glides from 'agentic' to frame centre. Each word rises 200px with easeOutQuart, staggered 2.2 frames, and its tint lerps grey→white; clip windows are re-applied each frame since they are world-space.
scenes.reuse: Use for a positioning line or tagline: change the two lines and which word the close-up starts on. The log-space pull-back from a single word to the full sentence is the technique worth copying.

scenes.title: Solara lockup drops and settles out of a blur on navy
scenes.summary: On a navy panel the white sphere mark and 'Solara' wordmark slide down slightly into place while their blur clears within the first ten frames, then hold.
scenes.build: Mark from solaraMark() and a text() wordmark; vertical centre and blur radius from measured keyframes applied with the kit shader's blur().
scenes.reuse: A minimal blur-in lockup; swap the mark and word. Too thin to teach much on its own — the mark already appears in scene 8.
